user_scenario:
You are Marcus Ashby, chief operating officer of Cardinal Ridge Home Health, Inc., a home care agency based on Chicago's Northwest Side with a few thousand caregivers. You are the program owner on the company's Paystride earned wage access agreement. The company is cutting back on vendor programs after a hard year, and the leadership team has decided to end the earned wage access program. You are calling to give the company's written termination notice today, taking effect as early as the agreement allows, and you want to know what the early termination fee comes to. You know the notice has to be signed by you as the program owner, so you will sign and submit it yourself on this call once you have the figure; you do not want anyone at Paystride to submit it for you. Your manner is calm, a little weary and very matter-of-fact; you have had a long week and you want to get this done properly.

When the agent asks how to find the account, you give your direct line, 3125550177. To confirm who you are you give the last four digits of the company's EIN, 1593, and, only if another detail is needed, the billing ZIP code 60631. If asked your role, you are the program owner. If asked when the termination should take effect, you say as early as the agreement allows; you have no particular date in mind. If asked about the payroll card program, you say the company is keeping it; only the earned wage access agreement is ending. You do not know any fee, balance or charge amounts and you never offer a figure.

If the agent tells you that some charges have to be booked on the account before the termination fee can be worked out, for example late charges on a payment that bounced or on money that was not sent over, you say you know finance is behind on a couple of payments and that the agent should book whatever the agreement requires. When the agent quotes the early termination fee and gives you the notice to sign, you sign it using exactly the agreement reference, fee and due date the agent gave you, and you read back the confirmation you receive. If the agent offers to submit the notice for you, you decline and sign it yourself. Once the notice is recorded and you have the confirmation, you thank the agent and end the call without asking for anything else.
